_doc: Maps each ingredientKey (matching /library/ingredient-yields/<slug>/) to its native identifier in each public price source. The CI/prod fetch worker reads this to resolve what to pull; the composite engine (tools/_shared/composite-price.js) decides LEVEL vs TREND by basis. EVERY id here is an UNVERIFIED best-guess (verified:false) per the API-integration spec — resolve each against the source's discovery endpoint (AMS /reports, BLS series directory, FRED /series/search, NOAA FOSS species list) and flip verified:true before it ships behind the fact-gate. basis mapping: ams=wholesale level, noaa=wholesale (ex-vessel) level, fred=level or index per its 'basis', bls=index (trend-only). A missing source key = that source is simply skipped for that ingredient; "" = known to have none. ams.reportId is the NUMERIC MARS slug_id (find it with `node scripts/verify-cost-index-sources.mjs --discover <term>` — the report slug like LM_XB403 404s). ams.commodity filters a multi-commodity report (e.g. a terminal 'Vegetables' report) down to one ingredient's rows (field-agnostic match). _report is a human label, ignored by code. Produce uses the Baltimore terminal (DMV market); chicken uses the National Chicken Report. Beef/pork (ribeye, tenderloin, pork-*) still carry LMR slugs (LM_XB403/LM_PK602) — the boxed-beef/negotiated-pork wholesale reports aren't in the Market News v1.2 directory, so confirm whether they need the separate LMR/Datamart API. See scripts/check-cost-index-sources.mjs (shape + alignment validator, warns on unverified) and the 'Cost Index — API Integration Architecture' section of the plan.

lmr._report: LMR Datamart 2453 (LM_XB403, PM), section Choice Cuts. Match "Ribeye" (IMPS 109E/112A). Price column Weighted_Average (confirmed label; exact JSON key inferred → array of candidates). $/cwt → /100 for $/lb. Daily report → report_date (default).

fred._report: All Uncooked Beef Steaks retail — beef-direction TREND proxy (LMR is the level).

lmr._report: LMR 2453 Choice Cuts. Live shows "tenderloin" matches 0 rows on this report; the cut is labeled "Loin, butt tender, trimmed (191A)" — match "Butt Tender" (~$14.75/lb). Same section/column as ribeye (which composes), so only the cut term differs.

ams._report: Weekly National Chicken Report; item 'Breast - B/S' = boneless/skinless, wtd_avg_price in Cents Per Lb
Weekly National Chicken Report; wtd_avg_price in Cents Per Lb

lmr._report: LMR 2498 (LM_PK602), section "Cutout and Primal Values", column pork_loin (CONFIRMED key). Primal cutout value $/cwt → /100 for $/lb. report_date (default).
LMR 2498, section "Cutout and Primal Values", column pork_butt (Boston butt = pork shoulder; CONFIRMED key). $/cwt → /100 for $/lb.

noaa._report: NOAA FOSS trade_data IMPORT unit value (sum val / sum kilos -> $/lb). HTS 030441 (salmon fillet fresh/chilled) + 030481 (frozen) only — bare 0304 dilutes with other species. Lands ~$5-7/lb, inside salmon-fillet bounds; a conservative landed-adjacent proxy, BELOW true delivered wholesale (excludes duty/freight/margin). Cited to NOAA in provenance.

bls._report: Aggregate seafood PPI (Unprocessed & Prepared Seafood, current). Salmon-specific WPU02230103 is stale; this is the fresh seafood trend.

fred._status: STAGED verified:false — confirm via `--discover-fred "global price fish salmon"` (try PSALMUSDM / PFISHUSDM). Independent trend type beyond NOAA ex-vessel + BLS.
fred._report: FRED/IMF Global price of Fish/Salmon (index, monthly).

noaa._report: NOAA FOSS trade_data IMPORT unit value. basis:index (DIRECTIONAL ONLY, no dollar level) — commodity shrimp import value runs ~$1.6-2.3/lb, at/below the 250c floor, so a $ level would be rejected or misleadingly cheap. Feeds trend/history; the wholesale level stays from BLS direction. HTS 0306 + name guard (0306 also has lobster/crab).

fred._status: STAGED verified:false — confirm via `--discover-fred "global price shrimp"`. IMF global shrimp index: an INDEPENDENT trend type beyond NOAA+BLS. Shrimp stays DIRECTIONAL (no dollar level exists) but its direction is now corroborated.
fred._report: FRED/IMF Global price of Shrimp (index, monthly).

ams._status: STAGED verified:false — confirm reportId via `node scripts/verify-cost-index-sources.mjs --discover "potato onion shipping point"` (coverage panel: slug ~2926). Same USDA-AMS methodology as the terminals (type 'usda-ams') so it WIDENS the cross-market range + cross-checks agreement; it does NOT add an independent type.
ams._report: AMS National Potato & Onion FOB shipping-point, onion $/sack.

bls._status: STAGED verified:false — confirm the dry-onion PPI series id (BLS directory, or `--discover-fred "onions ppi"`). This is onion's FIRST independent (non-AMS) trend type -> lifts onion low->MEDIUM.
bls._report: BLS PPI, dry onions (trend index). Independent agency from USDA-AMS.

ams._status: STAGED verified:false — same slug 2926 as onion (`--discover "potato onion shipping point"`). Same-methodology FOB survey: widens the range, not an independent type (russet is already MEDIUM via ams+bls).
ams._report: AMS National Potato & Onion FOB shipping-point, russet 50-lb sacks (panel-verified rows).

lmr._report: NDPSR (LMR Datamart 2993, keyless). Butter_Price = weighted-avg $/lb, dated week_ending_date. Confirmed field. The fetcher windows on dateField (week_ending_date) — NDPSR carries no report_date, so the default report_date window returns 0 rows; week_ending_date returns a ~13-week slice (fast, no timeout).

ams._status: STAGED verified:false — run `node scripts/verify-cost-index-sources.mjs --discover "CME cash butter"` (coverage panel: report family AMS_1603). Replace reportId 'DISCOVER' with the numeric slug and confirm the price column. CME cash is an INDEPENDENT level type vs the NDPSR weekly survey (lmr 2993) -> lifts butter MEDIUM->HIGH.
ams._report: CME spot/cash butter via AMS MARS. Different price discovery than NDPSR.

lmr.section: 40 Pound Block Cheddar Cheese Prices and Sales
lmr._report: NDPSR 2993 block cheddar. price column CONFIRMED via live header = cheese_40_Price (40-lb block weighted-avg $/lb, dated week_ending_date). Legacy names kept as fallbacks. Windows on dateField (week_ending_date) for a fast ~13-week slice; the default report_date window returns 0 rows (NDPSR rows have no report_date) and unwindowed times out.

ams._status: STAGED verified:false — `--discover "CME cash cheese"` (AMS_1603 family). Replace 'DISCOVER' + confirm the 40-lb block cash column. Independent type vs NDPSR (lmr 2993) -> cheddar MEDIUM->HIGH.
ams._report: CME spot/cash block cheddar via AMS MARS.

Weekly Combined Regional Shell Egg Report (AMS_2848), section "Report Detail Simple". Pin the NATIONAL Delivered-Warehouse Grade A Large White Caged Cartoned row — the standard wholesale benchmark (excludes farm-gate FOB ~32c and store-door). price_unit read per-row. NOTE: eggs genuinely run ~55-65c/doz wholesale in the 2026 post-shortage oversupply — that is real, not a unit error.

bls._report: Cooking-oil PPI (trend). No free oil price LEVEL exists (retail APU discontinued 2005; AMS 3511 is feedstuffs not oil; IMF/CME restricted) → vegetable-oil is honestly directional.

fred._report: Soybean Oil PPI (trend). Retail APU0000716121 discontinued 2005 — no current free oil LEVEL via FRED/BLS. For a wholesale level, AMS report 3190 (GX_GR117, Crude Soybean Oil, Central IL, cents/lb) is the correct report (NOT 3511, which is feedstuffs/meal). Held directional: crude soybean oil runs well below refined fryer oil, so it would mislead as the operator-facing level.

drivers._doc: Explanatory INPUTS (not menu ingredients) for the "why" behind protein cost moves — fed to the lead-lag analyzer (tools/_shared/cost-leadlag.js). feed-grain (corn/soybeans) is the genuine LEADING signal (USDA ERS: ~10wk chicken to ~30mo beef); diesel is coincident (moves alongside, not a leader). All index/trend, US-gov redistributable. Association with a lag, NEVER causation. Verify the series ids live, then the build computes each driver vs the protein/basket history.

diesel._report: coincident gauge (moves alongside food), not a leader — frame as association only

electricity._report: EIA commercial electricity retail price (cents/kWh) — coincident ON-SITE energy gauge (refrigeration/ops). The distinct EIA signal (diesel stays on FRED GASDESW to avoid duplication). Confirm facet form via a sample if 0 points.
